title: Roasted Gurbell with Crispy Air-Fryer Potato Wedges
summary: A Mediterranean-style whole roasted grouper with marjoram, thyme, paprika, garlic and lemon, served with crispy seasoned potato wedges.

steps.heading: Prepare the potatoes
steps.text: Wash and scrub the potatoes, then cut them into evenly sized wedges, about 2 cm thick.
Soak the wedges in cold water for {timer:20-30|soak}.
Drain and dry the wedges extremely well with a clean kitchen towel.
In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, plain flour, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, black pepper, salt and cayenne pepper for the wedges.
Add the potatoes and toss until evenly coated.

steps.heading: Prepare the fish
steps.text: Make sure the fish is scaled and gutted. Pat it completely dry, inside and outside.
Make two or three shallow diagonal cuts on each side of the fish.
Make the seasoning oil: mix together the olive oil, marjoram, thyme, paprika, oregano, black pepper and salt for the fish.
Rub the seasoning oil over both sides of the fish, including inside the cuts.
Season the cavity: add the dried garlic powder, two or three of the lemon slices, a pinch of thyme and marjoram, and a little salt and pepper.

steps.heading: Cook the potato wedges
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to {temp:200} for {timer:3}.
Arrange the wedges in a single layer without overcrowding. Cook for {timer:25-30|wedges}, turning them at 10 and 20 minutes.
Once cooked, finish the wedges with the lemon zest, a tiny squeeze of lemon juice and salt to taste.

steps.heading: Roast the Gurbell
steps.text: Fully preheat the oven to {temp:210/190}, with a rack in a high position, but not the very top. Lightly oil a roasting tray.
Place the fish in the roasting tray and put it on the high rack. Roast uncovered, without turning, for about {timer:20-25|fish}. Start checking after 18 to 20 minutes.
If the skin browns too quickly, cover it loosely with foil towards the end.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.text: Serve half the fish per person, with a generous portion of the potato wedges, fresh lemon wedges and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

tips: These timings are for a fish of about 800 g to 1 kg. The cooking time can differ considerably with the weight and thickness of the fish.
Marjoram and thyme are lovely with fish, while paprika gives the skin colour and warmth.
Keep the dried garlic mainly inside the cavity, so that it does not burn on the exposed skin.
